clue.text: The down-to-earth guy put cats' hair to use

indicators.note: putting letters to use here means working them into a new arrangement

parts.note: the possessive apostrophe adds no letter

explanation.surface: Someone finds a practical purpose for the fur their cats shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to use' signals rearranging PUT CATS HAIR. 'Down-to-earth' looks like praise for a sensible man, but it describes someone who literally drops to the ground from a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A skydiver descends from aircraft to the ground, so he is literally a man who comes down to earth.

clue.text: Near-crazy songwriter

indicators.note: crazy suggests the letters of the word before it are jumbled about

explanation.surface: A composer who is almost out of his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' signals rearranging NEAR. Thomas Arne was the 18th-century English composer of Rule, Britannia!
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Arne composed songs and stage music, including the patriotic anthem Rule, Britannia!

clue.text: A piano harbours such pests

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
to harbour a fugitive is to conceal or hide him

explanation.surface: Greenfly or similar insects are found living inside a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphids, also called greenfly, are sap-sucking insects that damage garden plants.

clue.text: Cut the poor journalist

definitions.meaning: to chop roughly with heavy blows
a writer of mediocre, churned-out copy

explanation.definitionFit: To hack is to chop crudely, and a hack is a jobbing reporter who produces dull writing.

clue.text: Twisting or not, is certainly crooked

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the preceding letters are distorted into a new order

explanation.surface: A debate over whether something is bent, ending with a firm verdict that it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'certainly crooked' signals rearranging OR NOT IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Torsion is the action of turning or wrenching something about its axis.

clue.text: Stage favourites given write-up

indicators.note: in a down clue a write-up has the word written upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: teacher's pets are favourites

explanation.surface: Theatre stars receive a glowing review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given write-up' tells you, in a down answer, to write PETS from bottom to top. 'Stage' looks like the theatre but means a phase.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is one stage in a process or progression.

clue.text: He's on board to deal with complaints

definitions.text: He's on board to deal with complaints

parts.words: He's on board to deal with complaints
parts.note: reads like a company official handling customer grievances, but board means a vessel and complaints are illnesses

explanation.definitionFit: A medical officer travels with a vessel's crew and passengers to treat their ailments.

clue.text: Floored, so being reprimanded

definitions.meaning: lying on the floor covering, literally
summoned before a superior to be scolded

explanation.definitionFit: Literally the phrase means lying on the rug; idiomatically it means facing a telling-off from the boss.

clue.text: Putting on too much weight!

parts.note: sounds like getting fat, but means placing too heavy a burden on a vehicle or circuit

explanation.definitionFit: Burdening something beyond its capacity is the literal sense of piling excess weight onto it.

clue.text: Like a glass — and it could make parents rant

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged to make a new word, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A see-through vessel whose contents would make any parent fume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' links the answer and PARENTS RANT as anagrams of each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear glass lets light pass through, so one can see through it.

clue.text: Only a few lines for one of the lesser characters

definitions.meaning: a short note or message of correspondence
a lower-case letter of the alphabet, as opposed to a capital

explanation.definitionFit: A brief note is a little piece of correspondence, and a lower-case character is a minuscule rather than a capital.

clue.text: About four the man hums with industry!

indicators.note: about means around, so the man goes around the number

parts.note: he is the pronoun for the man
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone at a quarter to four is buzzing with productive energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A beehive is a busy, buzzing place, and figuratively any scene of bustling activity.

clue.text: Soft butter — it's for a baby

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft
a ram butts with its head, so it is a butter

explanation.surface: Gentle dairy spread suitable for an infant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the spread but a thing that butts.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby carriage is pushed along with an infant lying in it.

clue.text: Turned up mid-afternoon to inspect range

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the word up is read backwards
mid points to the central letter of the word afternoon

parts.note: to view something is to inspect it

explanation.surface: Someone appeared halfway through the afternoon to look over a cooking stove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' reverses UP to PU; 'mid' takes R, the centre of AFTERNOON. 'Range' looks like a kitchen stove but means scope.
explanation.definitionFit: Purview is the scope or extent of one's authority or concern.

clue.text: Boundaries, all going in different directions

indicators.note: going in means entering, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: W and S are the compass points west and south

explanation.surface: Borders where everything heads off every which way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going in' places ALL between W and S, two different compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Walls enclose and divide spaces, marking where one area ends.

clue.text: Pass around unattended army officer

indicators.note: around signals that one word surrounds the other

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
lone means alone, without company

explanation.surface: A military commander slips past without an escort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals a container. 'Pass' looks like a verb, moving past, but it is a noun: a gap through the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonel is a senior commissioned rank, commanding a regiment.

clue.text: Water-course where a trainee has to follow vessel

indicators.note: the pieces come after the container word in the answer

parts.note: a can is a vessel for holding liquid
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A path along the river where an apprentice must trail a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to follow' puts A and L after CAN. 'vessel' suggests a boat on the water but means a container. L plates mark learner drivers in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal is an artificial waterway cut for boats or irrigation.

clue.text: A novelist's long tale with point

parts.note: a saga is a long story
N for north, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A writer of fiction produces an epic story with a moral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' looks like a story's purpose but is a compass point. Françoise Sagan wrote Bonjour Tristesse.
explanation.definitionFit: Françoise Sagan was a French author of novels such as Bonjour Tristesse.

clue.text: Note low return results in ruin

parts.note: D is a note of the musical scale

indicators.note: return means come back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.surface: A poor financial result leads to disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses MOO to OOM. 'low return' reads like a bad investment, but low is the cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Doom is a terrible fate, destruction from which there is no escape.

clue.text: Love mate — a real gem!

parts.note: love means nil in tennis, the letter O
a pal is a mate or friend

explanation.surface: A fond tribute to a friend who is a real treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is an iridescent precious stone.

clue.text: Go ahead after cash appeal

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the first in the answer

parts.note: p for penny or pence, a coin of cash
to lead is to go ahead of others

explanation.surface: Proceed once the fundraising request has been made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts LEAD behind P, a penny in British money.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead is to beg or entreat earnestly.

clue.text: Plan to be outstanding

definitions.meaning: to stick out beyond a surface

explanation.definitionFit: A project is a planned scheme, and to project is to jut out or protrude.

clue.text: The pleasure of French come down!

parts.note: de is the French word for of
to light is to alight or land, as a bird does

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at the joy of descending into France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come down' means LIGHT in the sense of a bird alighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Delight is great enjoyment or joy.

clue.text: Many get bad grades and they ask for assistance

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many

indicators.note: bad indicates the letters of the following word are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: Lots of students fail exams and seek help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges GRADES into ADGERS. Using C for 'many' is a crossword convention: a hundred is a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: People who cadge scrounge or beg favours or money from others.

clue.text: The young bounder!

parts.note: sounds like a youthful cad, but a bounder here is something that bounds, a hare, and the young one is its offspring

explanation.definitionFit: A leveret is a hare in its first year; hares move in leaps.

clue.text: Grants available in town slum-clearance programmes

indicators.note: in points to letters sitting inside the run of clue words that follows

explanation.surface: Funding is offered for urban redevelopment schemes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' tells you to find the answer within tOWN Slum.
explanation.definitionFit: To own a point is to admit or concede it, as in owning up.

clue.text: Send no end before dried up

indicators.note: no means without, so the following word is taken away from the one before

parts.note: taken as written
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: An urgent instruction to dispatch something before it withers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' removes the letters END from SEND, leaving S.
explanation.definitionFit: Sere is a literary word for withered or parched.

clue.text: Live unhappily in an area liable to flood

indicators.note: unhappily suggests the letters are in an unfortunate disordered state

explanation.surface: Living miserably on a floodplain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhappily' rearranges LIVE. A vlei is South African low ground that floods in the rainy season.
explanation.definitionFit: In South Africa a vlei is a low-lying marshy hollow that fills with water seasonally.

clue.text: Money put down before a deal is made

definitions.text: Money put down before a deal is made

parts.words: Money put down before a deal is made
parts.note: reads like a business deposit, but the deal is the dealing of cards in poker

explanation.definitionFit: In poker each player puts a stake into the pot before the cards are dealt.

clue.text: Concerning a holy man having nothing

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for saint
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Regarding a penniless monk.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means about or with regard to.

clue.text: The person to turn to if wanting to trace relations

definitions.text: The person to turn to if wanting to trace relations

parts.words: The person to turn to if wanting to trace relations
parts.note: relations means relatives, and tracing them means researching a family tree

explanation.definitionFit: A researcher of family history traces lines of descent and ancestry.

clue.text: Check again on accommodating particular individual

indicators.note: accommodating means housing or containing, so the pair of words surrounds the rest

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
taken as written
strict means exacting or particular
I is a single person, one individual

explanation.surface: Inspecting a fussy guest's room once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodating' signals a container, and 'again' with 'on' together make the outer pair. 'Check' looks like a verb, inspecting, but it is a noun here: a curb.
explanation.definitionFit: A restriction is a limit or curb placed on something.
